title: Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack

claims.claim: Two major blockchain analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprits in the $6.3bn hack of Binance.

evidence.quote: Two major blockchain analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprits in the $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.

claims.claim: The Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor, was identified with high confidence by TRM Labs and Chainalysis as the likely culprit in the Binance hack.

evidence.quote: The Lazarus Group, a North Korean hacking unit also known as TraderTraitor, was identified "with high confidence" by TRM Labs, as well as Chainalysis.

claims.claim: In 2014, Sony Pictures was targeted in a suspected North Korean hack following the Hollywood film The Interview, which involved a plot to assassinate Kim Jong Un.

evidence.quote: Though not financial, the nation's most spectacular suspected hack took place in 2014. The target: Sony Pictures, which had made the Hollywood film The Interview. The film involves a plot to assassinate Kim.

claims.claim: The FBI said last year that North Korea was responsible for the theft of $1.5bn on the Bybit exchange.

evidence.quote: Last year, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said North Korea was responsible for the theft of $1.5bn on the Bybit exchange.

claims.claim: North Korean hackers are suspected in the theft of $620m worth of cryptocurrency in 2022.

evidence.quote: North Korean hackers are also suspected in the theft of $620m worth of cryptocurrency in 2022.

claims.claim: Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said subsequent investigations uncovered additional points of breach in the cyberattack.

evidence.quote: "Our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said.

claims.claim: A Binance spokesperson said on Friday that some 80% of stolen assets have been secured, while the rest remains unaccounted for.

evidence.quote: Some 80% of stolen assets have been secured, a Binance spokesperson said on Friday, but the rest remains unaccounted for.
